scenes.tts: Deep nuclei that never reach the spinal cord still decide, in the classic model, whether a movement goes ahead. How? Their output neurons, in G P i, fire steadily. They hold the thalamus under constant inhibition, like a foot resting on a brake. Movement needs the brake lifted.
scenes.caption: Deep nuclei that never reach the spinal cord still decide, in the classic model, whether a movement goes ahead. How? Their output neurons, in GPi, fire steadily. They hold the thalamus under constant inhibition, like a foot resting on a brake. Movement needs the brake lifted.
scenes.visual: Seven boxes of the loop appear (cortex, striatum, GPe, GPi, STN, thalamus, SNc); GPi pulses steadily along a red inhibitory arrow onto a dimmed thalamus, tagged brake; then GPi dims and the thalamus brightens.
scenes.narration: Deep nuclei that never reach the spinal cord still decide, in the classic model, whether a movement goes ahead. How? Their output neurons, in GPi, fire steadily. They hold the thalamus under constant inhibition, like a foot resting on a brake. Movement needs the brake lifted.

scenes.tts: Two routes reach that brake. In the direct pathway, striatal neurons with D one receptors inhibit G P i. Give each excitatory link plus one, and each inhibitory link minus one. Then multiply along the route. Plus one, times minus one, times minus one, times plus one. The product is plus one. Two inhibitions in series give disinhibition.
scenes.caption: Two routes reach that brake. In the direct pathway, striatal neurons with D1 receptors inhibit GPi. Give each excitatory link +1, and each inhibitory link −1. Then multiply along the route. +1, times −1, times −1, times +1. The product is +1. Two inhibitions in series give disinhibition.
scenes.visual: The direct route lights up link by link with its sign beside each arrow; the product (+1)(-1)(-1)(+1) = +1 builds; striatum rises, GPi falls, thalamus rises, cortical drive up.
scenes.narration: Two routes reach that brake. In the direct pathway, striatal neurons with D1 receptors inhibit GPi. Give each excitatory link +1, and each inhibitory link −1. Then multiply along the route. +1, times −1, times −1, times +1. The product is +1. Two inhibitions in series give disinhibition.

scenes.tts: The indirect pathway has more steps. Striatal neurons with D two receptors inhibit G P e. G P e inhibits the subthalamic nucleus, S T N. The S T N excites G P i. Multiply again. Plus one, minus one, minus one, plus one, minus one, plus one. The product is minus one. This route ends up decreasing cortical drive.
scenes.caption: The indirect pathway has more steps. Striatal neurons with D2 receptors inhibit GPe. GPe inhibits the subthalamic nucleus, STN. The STN excites GPi. Multiply again. +1, −1, −1, +1, −1, +1. The product is −1. This route ends up decreasing cortical drive.
scenes.visual: Boxes reset to neutral; the indirect route lights up link by link with signs; the product builds to -1; GPe falls, STN rises, GPi rises, thalamus falls, cortical drive down.
scenes.narration: The indirect pathway has more steps. Striatal neurons with D2 receptors inhibit GPe. GPe inhibits the subthalamic nucleus, STN. The STN excites GPi. Multiply again. +1, −1, −1, +1, −1, +1. The product is −1. This route ends up decreasing cortical drive.

scenes.tts: Now add dopamine from the substantia nigra, pars compacta. In the classic model, it excites the D one direct neurons. It inhibits the D two indirect neurons. Exciting a plus one route raises cortical drive. Inhibiting a minus one route also raises it. Both actions push toward movement.
scenes.caption: Now add dopamine from the substantia nigra, pars compacta. In the classic model, it excites the D1 direct neurons. It inhibits the D2 indirect neurons. Exciting a +1 route raises cortical drive. Inhibiting a −1 route also raises it. Both actions push toward movement.
scenes.visual: SNc sends two dotted modulatory arrows, one marked excites onto the D1 chips, one marked inhibits onto the D2 chips; each case is tagged with its route sign and drive up; both point toward movement.
scenes.narration: Now add dopamine from the substantia nigra, pars compacta. In the classic model, it excites the D1 direct neurons. It inhibits the D2 indirect neurons. Exciting a +1 route raises cortical drive. Inhibiting a −1 route also raises it. Both actions push toward movement.

scenes.tts: So losing dopamine pushes both routes toward less movement. The direct route weakens. The indirect route strengthens. G P e is more inhibited, the S T N is released, and G P i fires more. The thalamus is held down harder. The model predicts akinesia, as in Parkinson's disease.

scenes.visual: Dopamine arrows removed from SNc; D1 dims, D2 brightens; GPe dims, STN brightens, GPi brightens, thalamus dims; the label the model predicts akinesia ends the scene.
scenes.narration: So losing dopamine pushes both routes toward less movement. The direct route weakens. The indirect route strengthens. GPe is more inhibited, the STN is released, and GPi fires more. The thalamus is held down harder. The model predicts akinesia, as in Parkinson's disease.

scenes.tts: This is a way to reason about the direction of a change. It is not a measured law of how firing rates add. And the model strains. In mice, calcium signals from both pathways rose around the start of an action. It also gives no account of rest tremor. Keep the rule: multiply the signs to predict direction, and remember it is a model.
scenes.visual: The loop with a note not a measured law; D1 and D2 chips both brighten together, tagged in mice both rise at action start; a rest tremor chip is marked not explained; the rule line closes the scene.
